concepts.title: Transport Network and Modes
concepts.definition: Transport is a service linking production with consumption through lines and nodes; its modes are land (roads and railways), water (inland and ocean), air and pipelines, each chosen by distance, weight, value and urgency of the goods moved.
concepts.key_idea: A network's worth lies in nodes and accessibility: the denser the links, the lower the friction of distance.

concepts.title: Roads: Length and Regional Shares
concepts.definition: The world's total motorable road length is only about 15 million km, of which North America accounts for about 33 per cent, with highway density there reaching about 0.65 km per sq km.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying the world road length by North America's percentage share gives its approximate road length in million km.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy107.txt road length (15 million km), North America share (33 per cent) and density 0.65 km per sq km

concepts.title: Railways, Waterways and Air Routes
concepts.definition: Railways carry heavy traffic on dense networks of Europe, Russia and North America, with trans-continental lines like the Trans-Siberian linking continents; inland and ocean waterways offer the cheapest bulk transport through canals like Suez and Panama, while airways serve long-distance high-value flows through great airports.
concepts.key_idea: Each trunk route overcame a natural barrier - the Trans-Siberian crossed the taiga, the Suez canal cut the Cape route - shortening world distance.

concepts.title: Communication Services
concepts.definition: Communication networks carry messages rather than matter: postal services form the land-based grid, telecom and satellite systems carry voice and data instantly, and the internet with undersea cables integrates the global economy.
concepts.key_idea: Mass media and cyberspace compress space so that information moves faster than any transport mode.
